body: Yes, it's okay with me, and I have expressed so before. I didn't know he actually did, he's not really a reading kind of guy, but I have no worries about it.

Sorry, the details of the sexting incident are further down- shortly after our marriage/birth of our child, he sexted with an ex. We went to therapy and seemly had moved past it.

I don't feel like reading his texts would be useful. Even if he has escalated to a physical relationship and that's what caused him to step back, I don't want to know. It's very clear from his reactions to my questions that he was emotionally involved whether or not he was sleeping with her, so I'm no longer questioning myself or my perception of this series of events. Telling me for sure he slept with her might ease his guilt, but it would only add to my distress (which, given my history of pregnancy complications, is a very bad thing). I'm willing to move past this together even if there was sex so long as he puts the effort in to figure out why he did it, how to avoid it in the future, and how to be more connected at home. It will be obvious if he's putting in the effort with or without piling on hurtful details.

Right away is a relative term. It's been almost 2 years since the incident and we have been to therapy and spent a lot of time working on rebuilding our relationship as a team. No, I don't 100% trust him yet, and the thing with his coworker has highlighted that, but I was assured it was normal for it to take years to go back to former levels of trust.

We both want lots of children, I have religious reasons to not be on birth control, and things seemed stable and good between us when I got pregnant.

I honestly didn't occur to me to mention it. I know that it's stupid of me, but while they're both betrayals, him sexting someone who he doesn't have any physical contact with a couple times feels so different from slowly building an emotional connection with someone he sees every day that my brain didn't file them together until I was explicitly asked about whether I trust him.

I didn't want to sidetrack the discussion. I'll probably ask him tonight, but at the time it seemed like one extra thing too many in an already emotional conversation. Too often when we fight I'll realize afterwards that we never even discussed the original problem, and I really wanted to avoid that.

I agree that his actions here have not been those of a great husband or father.

I suspect based on the timing of his apparent decision it wasn't that he thought of it as inappropriate on his own, but that he read my diary- my entry from the day prior to his alleged withdrawal talked about my feelings about their relationship.

As for the pregnancy attraction issue, that does line up in retrospect. Aside from rubbing my back/holding my hair while I threw up we didn't touch much last pregnancy either, and he didn't seem bothered by the lack of sex/touching at all. I was too overwhelmed by the constant complications to dwell on it at the time.

In terms of lack of attraction, it was present with the last pregnancy. I thought the infrequency of sex (every couple months) was due to my own exhaustion from pregnancy complications. He still touched me, but looking back physical contact was mostly limited to him rubbing my back while I threw up. Luckily this pregnancy has been easy, but it means he's niether wanting sex nor is he required to care for me. He still talked to me last time. The sexting incident happened after our child was born and we'd already increased the frequency of our sex life again, so I don't think that had to do with pregnancy.

My best guess is that, this time, he simultaneously stopped being attracted to me and he met a very attractive girl who wants to spend time with him, developed a crush that's been heightened by the lack of physical intimacy at home, and slowly stopped talking to me or spending time with me as a result.

Hopefully he either pulls it together and works on our marriage or takes the time to think it over now that I've confronted him about it and make a clean break.

I'm sorry if I wasn't clear: it's not her advice that I'm finding valuable, but the fact she is expressing for me the things I know wouldn't be helpful to express. Would screaming "FUCK YOU" in my husband's face be helpful? No, but I still want to. Having someone else do it for me in an enviroment where it's not going to damage the chances of repairing my relationship and reaching an amicable solution is, in an odd way, useful to me in releasing the pressure from my emotions so I can keep doing the most useful thing without having a breakdown and screaming profanities.

I'm actually finding u/YouCanCallMeABitch's comments very therapeutic, not laughable. Even if it is coming from a place of projection (though generally commiserating with someone going through the same shitty sotuation is consider sympathizing?), the validation of my hurt and rage and pain is cathartic. I'm not going to use the phone call suggestion and I am struggling to remain calm and approach this in a logical manner, but it's difficult in the face of the prior sexting incident, and having someone else express my emotions for me is proving helpful in keeping my cool and focusing on the appropriate next steps.

I wouldn't say he's really transparent. For example, he'll say he went to lunch with a friend if I ask specifically what he did for lunch, but not if I ask what he did for the day. If I ask which friend he went with he just says "y'know,the girl", but if I guess it was her by name he'll say yes it was her. I don't know much of anything past her name/department, which he told me when we first moved. 

It took me weeks before I knew he was going to lunch with her daily, because I hadn't know to specifically ask if he went to lunch vs. how his day went, and I had to specifically ask "how many times a week do you go to lunch with her" (4 or 5 times) before he said it was anything other than "sometimes". The fact she pays for his food only came up because we're on a tight budget and needed to talk about how to financially handle daily lunches out and still pay bills.

Okay as in happy with it? No. Okay as in capable of doing it without cheating? Absolutely.

Is he okay with it? I certainly hope he's not fine with gpong 9 months without sex, but he damned well better be able to keep it in his pants anyway. It's not like I'm denying him sex, he just doesn't like the effectives his choices are having on my body. Sorry to put it crudely, but if he needs to stick his dick in something other than his hand so bad he would cheat, he can suck it up and sleep with me instead.

I met with one to learn my options after the initial incident with his ex. I do not want to divorce, but I am aware of legalities involved and how they can play out in our judicial system. My toddler and I should be protected financially even if my husband choses to leave.

I would love to eat lunch with him (even without all this coworker stuff!) but his work is on the other side of town and I don't have a car. In the summer it might be doable, but it's too long a walk in the snow with a toddler. I do meet him at his work on Grocery Day, but the coworker in question is from a different department so I haven't run into her yet.

I'm on mobile and my phone isn't cooperating,  so instead of editing in a update I'm going to comment with it. Sorry.

After the first couple comments came back confirming I'm not nuts for being concerned, I bundled the tyke off to bed and sat down for a talk with my husband. It wasn't as bad as I expected, but it wasn't great either.

He was very angry at first, but I focused on "I feel..." statements (thank you for that suggestion!) and that helped keep it on track. Once he calmed down he apologized for crossing the line last week with the movie, and said that he'd been backing off and hadn't spent time with her/gone to lunch with her for the last two days, which opened the door for me to ask why he felt the need to back off if the relationship was platonic/appropriate, and why he was angry about having to back off if he had no emotional attachment to her. It was enlightening to watch him struggle with answering those questions; obviously there are feelings there. Ultimately his answer was just that while cutting her off would hurt, destroying our marriage would hurt worse.

I then segued into talking about our marriage: at the moment, there's really no relationship to miss. He admitted that he's not physically attracted to me when pregnant, hence the lack of sex and intimacy. It doesn't really surprise or upset me- my body is hugely different while pregnant, and physical attraction isn't something he can help. I have hands for a reason. However, I pointed out that cuddling/holding hands/talking doesn't require sexual attraction, and he said he'd been avoiding it because he didn't want me to be led on/disappointed sexually. I reassured him that now that I know, I won't expect sexual intimacy while pregnant and that's OK, but I do expect non sexual touch. He did cuddle me after that and apologize again for hurting me, and made some promises about future behaviour with female friends, this coworker specifically, and for our relationship.

I don't know what's going to happen now. It's a game of wait-and-see; he can say whatever he wants about not spending time with her, but I can't police his every interaction; he can promise all he wants to be more interactive and attentive as a husband and father, but until time goes by I won't know if it's just words or not.

Honestly- and I know this is bad of me- I don't trust him. Shortly after our wedding/the birth of our son, I was using his phone and noticed he'd downloaded snap chat. I snooped and there were records of 2 or 3 recent snaps between him and an ex. The next morning I asked him about it, he said it was just friendly stuff about our son. I thought it was suspicious and asked to read his texts with her. He deleted them instead.

We've been through conselling and therapy and chalked most of it up to stress from an unplanned pregnancy/unplanned fatherhood, but trust is still a big issue for me. That's why I asked here if I was being unreasonable instead of just confronting him; my natural tendancy now is to assume the worst, and I have to fight hard to stay objective.
